reviews.review:
I stayed away from this game for over a decade because of people harping on it's story and bugs. It is buggy even now. Sometimes the audio or the music will cut out. sometimes you can "die too fast" and will soft lock the game. Sometimes a quest audio will loop. These are annoying, but not 'run-stopping.' 

I found that the story was good, the reasoning was good and it was 'mass effect-y' enough for me to still enjoy this was part of the franchise. 

I think the biggest piece of unnecessary hate this game gets is "It's not as good as the trilogy."  I mean...it's not, but comparing a THREE GAME narrative arc to a single game that got slapped down before it got started isn't fair either. 

What I ended up comparing this game to in a much more realistic way is "narratively - does this game hold up to Mass Effect 1? - and I think it does. Andromeda was the first of an intended line. The characters were good enough and had more than enough depth for a first game in an intended franchise. It holds it own for sure and is worth a playthrough or two. 

I was going to end there, but another thing I think gets harped on too much is " Shapard vs Ryder"

Shepard =/= Ryder. Again, taking ME1 and Andromeda for comparison.
 
Shepard is an N7 turned Spectre for the Council tasked with hunting a rogue agent. Eventually discovering the greater threat to the galaxy.

Ryder is a Pathfinder tasked with founding new colonies using prototype AI trying to fill the shoes of his ex-N7 father with the lives of the entire initiative riding on his shoulders at the start of the game. 

Totally different jobs. Totally different (theoretical ) skill sets required. They shouldn't be compared and treated as separate entities. 

TLDR - The story is good, but the game is buggy. It does not deserve the hate it gets, but it is understandable why it get slapped for the technical issues it has had throughout the years.

I think the criticisms aimed at this game are only partly justified.  Disappointed that this was not a direct sequel to ME3 many gamers unfairly picked on the game just for existing.  

Is the storyline as grand as the Trilogy, no.  Are the characters as memorable, not really.  But it does have some pluses going for it.

It IS another Mass Effect game, and the only one we have after the trilogy.  Who knows when, or if, a more direct successor to the trilogy will arrive, especially with EA up for sale and Bioware weakened under their subjugation.  

I for one don't mind this game as the combat is just as good as, if not a little better, than ME3 and the lore is interesting, if a little painful to tease out.  I absolutely love the galaxy and system map's graphic fidelity and effects, while it's not for everyone it IS beautiful and is one of my favourite things in the game.

The biggest problems seem to be pacing and a lack of meaningful decisions that have a lasting impact, other than the endgame, that is.  After fixing up much of the jank that came with launch, and the ever brilliant work of the modding community, it's not that bad a play.  While criticised, I enjoy the abundance of cutscenes and see them as small episodes of a sci-fi show, as I'm sure they were intended to be.

So a recommended, and a plea not to be too hard on it until you have played through it at least once.
The EA Launcher, i just wont buy your games anymore.

A fun action game, most bugs from the initial release have been fixed, but the writing is still bad compared to the original trilogy, especially the world building. Space orcs as villains. Plot holes you can fly an arc through. Quests that go nowhere, big decisions that have zero consequences. Fun, if you don't care about this.
